title: docs: `os migrate duplicates` needs its row in the data-migration table, and the #8686 backfill guidance owes it the cross-reference the ruling asked for
body:
~~Blocked-by: #9342~~ — **RESOLVED 2026-08-18 by the PM seat.** #9342 delivered as PR #9429: measured as `+0/-3`, three deletions of one stale transcript line, in sections of `cli.mdx` that do not touch the data-migration table. ⇒ no textual overlap with this card's edit is possible, so this card is dispatchable now rather than after #9429 lands.

Follow-up to #8928, which ships `os migrate duplicates` — the operator-facing inventory of business identifiers the tenancy split already minted twice.

Two docs edits are owed, neither made in that PR because its declared file surface was `packages/cli/src/commands/**`:

1. **`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`** — the hand-written data-migration table (the one listing `os migrate files-to-references`, `os migrate value-shapes`, `os migrate summary-nulls`, `os migrate meta --stored`) has no row for the new command, and there is no section for it beneath. An operator command that is not in the operator docs is half-shipped. Suggested row, matching the voice of its siblings:

   | `os migrate duplicates` | Report business identifiers already minted twice across the organization partitions. Read-only inventory as JSON on stdout — never renumbers, and must be run BEFORE the #8686 backfill, which overwrites the evidence |

2. **The cross-reference the ruling asked for.** The 2026-08-16 maintainer ruling on #8928 carries it as a binding note: "operator guidance around the backfill cross-references this command once it exists." Wherever the #8686 / PR #8832 tenancy backfill is described for operators, that page should say that the report is run first — the `organization_id = NULL` marker the report reads is exactly what the repair overwrites, and the live-condition line (a `__global__` counter still standing beside an organization-scoped one) can never be produced again after the repair merges and deletes it.

Verified facts a writer can lean on, all pinned by tests in the #8928 PR:

- the command writes nothing at all, boot included (`duplicates.integration.test.ts` asserts the database is byte-identical after a full run);
- the *inventory* survives the backfill — the repair deliberately refuses to move a row whose identifier is already taken in the destination partition — but the *live condition* does not (`duplicates.pre-repair.test.ts` runs the real `backfillSeedTenancy` and measures both);
- output is always JSON on stdout; there is no `--json` flag and no human renderer, per the ruling's point 3.
